what.text: This page follows asylum seekers from the Democratic Republic of the Congo in the United States: people who have asked for international protection and are waiting for a decision.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 1947 asylum seekers from the Democratic Republic of the Congo in the United States, 1.2% of all asylum seekers from the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
Refugees from the Democratic Republic of the Congo, a separate group, live mostly in Uganda, Burundi, Zambia and Rwanda.

why.text: UCDP records armed conflict over the government of DR Congo in periods from 1996 to 2025, with M23 among the opponents.
It also records armed conflict with the Islamic State group from 2017 to 2025.

when.text: UNHCR's series for this group starts in 2000 at 145 asylum seekers.
The figure was at its highest, 4654, at the end of 2024; the main years of displacement in the data are 2018 to 2019 and 2021 to 2024.

how.text: The sources don't say which routes people took or where they live in the United States.
Asylum seekers are counted separately from refugees, as year-end totals for the United States only.
